# The Light That Outlasts the Night

## Scripture
"The night is nearly over; the day is almost here. So let us put aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light." — Romans 13:12

## Reflection
Tonight, step outside and look for the constellation Lyra—the Lyre, a small harp tucked between brighter neighbors. Its brightest star, Vega, shines with a cool blue-white radiance that has guided stargazers for millennia. Yet here’s what’s remarkable: Vega’s light left that star 25 years ago. What you see tonight is a ghost of the past, a delayed whisper of a sun that may have already shifted, burned, or dimmed.

We live in that same delay. We carry wounds that feel like yesterday, waiting for a dawn that seems stubbornly distant. But the apostle Paul reminds us that our night has an expiration date. Not a vague someday, but a guaranteed “almost here.” God’s light doesn’t travel to us slowly like starlight—it breaks in with the urgency of sunrise. Even now, in the middle of your darkest season, the morning is being prepared.

Vega’s light is beautiful, but it is old. The light of Christ is ahead of us, not behind. And it will outlast every shadow.

## Prayer
Father of the dawn, when the night feels long, remind us that your day is breaking. Help us to shed the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light—patient, expectant, and ready for the morning you have promised. Amen.
